scope_guards.d: Programme outputs, pledges and population estimates do not prove connectivity, equipment or skills for an exact household or parcel.
scope_guards.f: Tracker methodology and response metadata do not determine affordability or eligibility for an individual household or address.

Ofcom's Telecommunications Market Data Update was last updated on 23 July 2026 and the latest section covers Q1 2026.
UK fixed voice service revenues totalled £891.9 million in Q1 2026.
Q1 2026 fixed voice revenue was £49.5 million, or 5.3%, lower than the previous quarter.
Q1 2026 fixed voice revenue was £194.2 million, or 17.9%, lower year on year.
The UK had 20.7 million fixed lines at the end of Q1 2026, including PSTN, ISDN channels and managed VoIP connections.
The number of fixed lines fell by 757,000, or 3.5%, during Q1 2026.
Total fixed-originated call volume was 3.32 billion minutes in Q1 2026.
Fixed-originated call volume fell by 583 million minutes, or 14.9%, year on year in Q1 2026.
There were 29.4 million fixed broadband lines at the end of Q1 2026.
Fixed broadband lines increased by 282,000, or 1.0%, year on year by the end of Q1 2026.
Mobile telephony retail revenues totalled £3.57 billion in Q1 2026.
Mobile telephony retail revenues increased by £55.6 million, or 1.6%, year on year in Q1 2026.
Average monthly mobile retail revenue per subscriber was £13.10 in Q1 2026.
Average monthly revenue was £15.54 for post-pay mobile subscribers and £5.40 for pre-pay users in Q1 2026.
There were 90.6 million active mobile subscriptions excluding M2M at the end of Q1 2026.
Active mobile subscriptions excluding M2M increased by 881,000, or 1.0%, year on year by the end of Q1 2026.
Dedicated mobile broadband subscriptions totalled 5.2 million at the end of Q1 2026.
Dedicated mobile broadband subscriptions increased by 421,000, or 8.8%, year on year by the end of Q1 2026.
Mobile-originated voice call volume totalled 36.34 billion minutes in Q1 2026.
Mobile-originated voice call volume fell by 1.76 billion minutes, or 4.6%, year on year in Q1 2026.
Mobile calls to landlines totalled 6.07 billion minutes in Q1 2026, 7.2% lower year on year.
Mobile messages including SMS and MMS totalled 4.61 billion in Q1 2026.
Mobile messages fell by 1.25 billion, or 21.3%, year on year in Q1 2026.
Mobile data usage totalled 3,042 petabytes in Q1 2026.
Mobile data usage increased by 351 petabytes, or 13.1%, year on year in Q1 2026.
Active mobile subscriptions excluding M2M were about 0.5 million lower in Q1 2026 than the 91.1 million reported for Q4 2025.
The Digital Inclusion Innovation Fund was launched with £11.9 million to support local projects across the UK.
Within two months of Women’s Wellbeing one-to-one digital support, two women secured their first jobs.
Age UK delivered internet-confidence support in 13 communities across England.
Government reported a multi-department pilot to refurbish and donate end-of-life devices with the Digital Poverty Alliance.
Virgin Media O2's Community Calling programme was reported to have helped more than 32,000 people get online with free phones.
The One Year On report sets out a six-point plan for the next year and beyond.
The Telecoms Consumer Charter was agreed in February 2026 and includes commitments on surprise in-contract price rises, social tariffs and support for customers in financial difficulty.
Around 1.7 million UK households were reported not to have a laptop, tablet or desktop computer.
The Digital Inclusion Action Committee and three subcommittees were established in June 2025.
The Digital Inclusion Action Committee structure brought together 35 experts.
DSIT and Google were working with North East local councils to provide digital and AI skills training for more than 100 care leavers and their advisers.
The IT Reuse for Good Charter was launched in June 2025 with Good Things Foundation, VodafoneThree and Deloitte UK.
Industry pledges were reported to have connected or supported more than one million people through cheaper internet, free data, donated devices and local digital support.
The Digital Inclusion Innovation Fund supported 85 projects in England.
The Digital Inclusion Innovation Fund delivered £1.47 million to devolved governments for initiatives across the UK.
DSIT planned a comprehensive update of the Essential Digital Skills Framework during 2026.
A refreshed Essential Digital Skills Survey was scheduled to relaunch in 2027.
The government device-donation pilot had led to around 200 devices being donated to community centres, homelessness charities and individuals.
The government device-donation pilot was renewed until August 2026.
The report states that digital should not be the only option and that public services should provide supported offline routes where appropriate.
Ofcom's Communications Affordability Tracker page was last updated on 14 May 2026.
The April 2026 Communications Affordability Tracker was published as seven Power BI parts on Ofcom's page.
Ofcom's financial-vulnerability measure combines household income, working status and household size into three groups.
Ofcom gives examples in which income below £10,400, or £36,400–£51,999 for a household of at least six people, can fall in the most financially vulnerable group.
In October 2025, 36% of tracker respondents either did not know or refused to provide household-income information.
